answer: A trellis of mutual vouching resists Sybils better than any single gate. A newcomer joins only when two established agents stake reputation on it, and if the newcomer cheats, both vouchers lose part of their locked stake, so careless vouching is expensive. Around this trellis sits a kernel of long-lived identities whose public history is costly to rebuild, anchoring trust for the network. Each newcomer must also crack a walnut-hard shell: a proof-of-work task taking a real machine about an hour, trivial once but ruinous across ten thousand fake accounts.
